gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of UV-Vis ATR and Raman (and optionally fluorescence) spectra from the same sampling spot, synchronised to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration block with block scaling so no method dominates. The fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.)
Yeast-specific metabolite targets and their concentration ranges are not covered by the supplied material; the bioprocess examples name glucose, acetate and lactate generically.
Measuring Broth optical-density range over the run: It decides whether transmission-type geometries stay viable or a short-path ATR geometry is required.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs by rearranging data into a new matrix where variables from different sources are placed one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing whether combining multiple spectroscopic inputs via low-level fusion improves monitoring compared to single methods. Careful evaluation of each dataset's contribution remains necessary.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The reviewed literature discusses general or different chemical matrices rather than yeast fermentation, so transferability across matrices and scales is uncertain.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
